messages.text: . ! status in a session should be cleared after the session is focused

Please answer the following questions.

Client: TUI dashboard (mj)
Status: Awaiting input / blocked
Other: i just know it's marked with ! (at this writing d8443f17cb24506c5ee26277fcf319f4 is an example)

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The dashboard tracks "read" status with a per-session read point (`viewed_through_event_ordinal`), not a yes/no flag. Opening a session moves that point forward to the latest event, and the change is saved as a read receipt.
- That only clears states that are worked out from unread events. A marker for a pending question or a warning may depend on other data that focusing never changes. That is the main idea the child is testing.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

A child agent is working out which state draws the `!` on session `d8443f17…` and why focusing does not clear it. I'll report back when it finishes.

The `!` on session `d8443f17…` is not a stale status. The marker is designed to stay until one of the session's child agents gets an answer to its question, and focusing the parent does not answer it. **Confirmed** from the session data and the code.

**Why it stays:**
- The parent session itself is idle. It has no pending question and no unread output. Its read point is already at the latest event (274515).
- One of its running child agents, `9645b51a…` (`6542-m1b-producer-repairs`), has an unanswered question (`elicitation-1`). The question asks whether direct negative facts can prove non-implementation on their own, or whether completeness flags must gate both branches.
- A parent row shows `!` (Waiting) when any active child has a pending question. This is on purpose. The comment at `mj-tui/src/session_view.rs:169-172` says child agents have no row of their own, so without this nothing would show that the child needs you.
- Focusing a session only moves its read point forward (`acknowledge_chat`, `mj-cli/src/dashboard.rs:1482`). It never clears questions or failures. The "mark read" notice states the same rule: "questions and failures stay flagged" (`mj-tui/src/dashboard_sessions.rs:1228`).

**A second `!` on the same row:** after the title there is a separate warning, "! Recovery copy … old". The last checkpoint failed on an unsupported untracked file type under `bifrost/.mj/lanes/6409-m4e1b/`. The last good copy is from 2026-10-22 05:00 UTC. That warning clears only after a checkpoint succeeds (`mj-tui/src/render/sessions.rs:1848`). Focusing has no effect on it either.

**My recommendation:** don't clear the marker when you focus the session. For a parent, it is the only sign that a child agent is waiting for you, so clearing it on focus would hide an open question. These changes would fix the confusion instead:
1. Make the parent row say which child has a question, for example "child 6542-m1b… has a question". `DashboardState::subagent_question` (`mj-tui/src/dashboard_sessions.rs:881`) already gets this information.
2. Use a different glyph for the recovery warning. Right now both states draw `!` (`mj-chat/src/theme.rs:747,768`).
3. Possibly: stop flagging a parent as Waiting when the child's question is non-blocking. This question says "Work can continue while you answer". Whether a non-blocking question should count as "needs you" is your call.

If you do want "seen but unanswered" to look different from "unseen", that is a larger change: it adds a third state for the row.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The dashboard works out a session's attention level from several sources: unread events, its own pending questions, failures, and its child agents' pending questions. Only the first one depends on what you have viewed.
- A row's level is the most urgent of its own state and its children's (`attention_level`, `session_view.rs:173`). So an idle parent can show Waiting because of work you can't see from its row.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Which of these changes do you want, if any? I haven't changed anything yet.

after.text: did the parent not see that child stopped w question?  child statuses should be surfaced to parent not to human

I agree with your design position. For a child agent, its "user" is the parent agent. The child's question about how to prove non-implementation is the kind of thing the parent can answer from its own
